title: TrackSpec
description: Wreckfest Track Generator track specification: metadata, the user's sketch (canvas coordinates) and build options. Cross-field rules live in track-rules.json.

slug.title: Track id
slug.description: Track and mod id: 3-24 characters, lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

Id.description: Identifier of a sketch element (route, crossing or jump), unique within its list.

RouteRef.description: A route: "main" for the main loop, otherwise the id of an alternative route.

Point.title: Point
Point.description: A point in canvas coordinates (x right, y down).

Canvas.title: Canvas
Canvas.description: Size of the drawing canvas the sketch coordinates refer to.

MainLoop.title: Main loop
MainLoop.description: The main loop stroke: a closed polyline. The last point joins the first; don't repeat the first point.

StartFinish.title: Start/finish
StartFinish.description: Start/finish marker on the main loop and the driving direction. If omitted, the first main-loop point is used, heading towards the second.

headingDeg.title: Heading
headingDeg.description: Driving direction in degrees on the canvas: 0 = +x (right), 90 = +y (down).

Attachment.title: Attachment
Attachment.description: Where an alternative route joins the main loop: a canvas point on the loop and/or a parameter along it (0 = start/finish, increasing in driving direction, < 1).

AltRoute.title: Alternative route
AltRoute.description: An alternative-route stroke. It must leave and rejoin the main loop (start and end attachments).

id.description: Route id; "main" is reserved for the main loop.

CrossingType.title: Crossing type
CrossingType.description: bridge: one branch goes over the other; flat: an at-grade intersection.

BranchRef.title: Branch
BranchRef.description: One branch through a crossing: the route plus, optionally, the parameter along it (needed to tell the two passes of a figure-of-eight apart).

Crossing.title: Crossing
Crossing.description: Annotation for a place where the track crosses itself.

over.description: For a bridge: the branch that goes over.

route.description: Route the jump is on (default: main).

bidirectional.title: Bidirectional
bidirectional.description: Ramp drivable in both directions (needed to keep the jump in the reverse layout).

ElevationMarker.title: Height marker
ElevationMarker.description: A height marker on a route. With elevation "custom" it sets the absolute road height there (the profile is interpolated between markers); with a preset it adds a smooth bump of this height on top of the preset terrain.

route.description: Route the marker is on (default: main).

heightM.title: Height (m)
heightM.description: Road height at the marker in metres: absolute with custom elevation, an offset from the preset terrain otherwise.

ImportedPoint.title: Imported centreline point
ImportedPoint.description: A point of an imported centreline in metres: x east, y north, z up (relative to datumM), and the road's cross-slope.

bankDeg.title: Camber (degrees)
bankDeg.description: Cross-slope: positive raises the driver's left edge above the right one.

widthM.title: Road width (m)
widthM.description: The tarmac's width at this point, centred on it (measured real widths; tools/real_tracks_data/measure_width.py). Without it the road is options.widthM wide.

MetrePoint.title: Point (metres)
MetrePoint.description: A point in the imported track's frame: metres, x east, y north.

Heightfield.title: Heightfield
Heightfield.description: Ground heights at the nodes of a regular grid, in the imported track's frame and datum: z[j * (nx + 1) + i] is at x = originX + i * cellM, y = originY + j * cellM.

WoodlandArea.title: Woodland area
WoodlandArea.description: A woodland polygon (metres, imported frame): the builder plants its trees inside it.

Lake.title: Lake
Lake.description: Open water inside the terrain (metres, imported frame): a flat water surface at levelM over the polygon; the terrain under it lies below that level.

levelM.description: Water surface height, relative to datumM.

NamedSpot.title: Named spot
NamedSpot.description: A named place along the imported centreline.

sM.description: Distance along the centreline from point 0 (the start/finish line), metres.

KerbOverride.title: Kerb override
KerbOverride.description: Real-world kerbs and track-limit strips at one corner of an imported track (from OSM, LIDAR or a track guide), overriding the builder's geometric placement (apex kerb inside, exit kerb outside, a green strip beyond the exit kerb on fast corners) at the corner nearest sM.

sM.description: Distance along the centreline of the corner (its named way's middle), metres.

entry.description: Kerb on the outside before the turn-in.

apex.description: Kerb on the inside at the apex.

exit.description: Kerb on the outside from the apex to the exit.

green.description: Green track-limit strip beyond the exit kerb.

source.description: Where this comes from (e.g. a track guide's URL).

HorizonProfile.title: Horizon profile
HorizonProfile.description: The distant skyline seen from the start line, beyond the far ground (from a regional DTM): per azimuth step, clockwise from north (+y), the highest terrain's elevation angle and whether the horizon there is open sea. The builder paints the #horizon texture from it (e.g. Snowdonia from Anglesey).

ImportedAltLayout.title: Imported alternative layout
ImportedAltLayout.description: Another real layout that shares the base scene: the main centreline with one section replaced by this branch. The branch is open, in driving order, and starts and ends on the main centreline (its first and last points are snapped to the nearest main points). The layout's lap is the branch, then the main centreline from the branch end round to the branch start. Without startFinish it shares the main start/finish line and grid (the lap must then pass the main line); with it, the layout has its own line and grid there.

id.description: Layout id (also the layout's scene name suffix); not main.

centreline.description: The branch from where it leaves the main centreline to where it rejoins it, points about 1-10 m apart.

startFinish.description: The layout's own start/finish line (some circuits time each layout at a different line): the point is projected onto the layout's lap, the grid starts there and the lap is counted from it. Omit it to share the main line.

ImportedTrack.title: Imported track
ImportedTrack.description: A real-world track: the exact centreline (closed, in driving order, point 0 on the start/finish line) with per-point heights and camber, plus optionally the surrounding terrain, woodland and named places. It replaces the drawn main loop, and the lap length is the centreline's.

datumM.description: Height above sea level of z = 0 (informational).

centreline.description: Closed centreline, points about 1-10 m apart; don't repeat the first point.

terrain.description: The surrounding ground. Without it the ground away from the road is level at the mean road height.

lakes.description: Lakes and ponds (e.g. Oulton Park's lake): flat water over the terrain.

kerbs.description: Per-corner kerb and track-limit overrides from real data; corners without one get the geometric placement.

mainLayoutName.description: Display name of the main centreline's layout when there are alternative layouts (e.g. International).

altLayouts.description: Further real layouts sharing the base scene (e.g. Anglesey's Coastal beside the International). Each gets its own layout (start points, checkpoints, AI routes).

seaLevelM.description: Sea surface height (relative to datumM) when the ground runs down to the sea: terrain below it is under water and the far ground becomes sea.

ImportedPits.title: Imported pits
ImportedPits.description: The real circuit's pit lane, pit wall, pit buildings, paddock, grandstands, bridges and gantries (metres, imported frame; from OSM and LIDAR, tools/real_tracks/pits). The builder lays the pit lane and its wall, places stock buildings, paddock props and grandstands on the footprints and the start lights, bridges and gantries at their real positions over the road.

PitLane.title: Pit lane
PitLane.description: A pit lane beside the main centreline, in the driving direction. closed: fenced off at both ends where the pit wall ends (the lane is scenery); drivable: open at its entry and exit (never on the AI route).

side.description: Side of the main centreline (driving direction).

PitLaneMode.title: Pit lane mode
PitLaneMode.description: closed: fenced off at both ends (scenery); drivable: open at its entry and exit, never on the AI route.

PitWall.title: Pit wall
PitWall.description: The pit wall between the track and the lane: continuous from sM[0] to sM[1] along the main centreline.

PitBuilding.title: Pit building
PitBuilding.description: A real building (or grandstand) footprint with its height and the direction its front faces (towards the nearest road).

facing.description: Unit vector from the footprint towards the road it faces.

PitGantry.title: Gantry or bridge
PitGantry.description: A structure over the road at sM along a route: the start lights, a bridge, a footbridge or an advertising gantry.

route.description: main, or an alternative layout's id.

topM.description: The real structure's top above the road (LIDAR), metres.

Sketch.title: Sketch
Sketch.description: The drawn layout, in canvas coordinates. The geometry service turns it into a spline scaled to the lap length.

imported.description: A real-world track (tools/import_real_track.py). Replaces the drawn main loop; use elevation "imported".

Walls.title: Walls
Walls.description: Wall type; none means open run-off.

Elevation.title: Elevation
Elevation.description: flat, gentle and hilly are seeded terrain presets (height markers add bumps on top); custom is flat ground shaped only by the height markers; imported takes the road heights, camber and terrain from sketch.imported (real tracks).

Environment.title: Environment
Environment.description: Environment preset (stock textures and props). parkland: lush grass, deciduous woods and grass banks. coastal: open, windswept coastal grassland with gorse, rocks along the shore, stone walls and the sea. airfield: a flat, open former airfield: short dry grass, few trees, arable fields beyond, a low horizon. arid: dry northern-Spain scrubland, sand and rock, a few pines, bare hills.

Weather.title: Weather
Weather.description: Stock weather (time-of-day) slot. Each environment preset maps a slot to a stock .weat (e.g. fields/fields08_midday1.weat). To be confirmed against game data per preset.

lapLengthKm.title: Lap length (km)
lapLengthKm.description: Target lap length; the sketch is scaled to match. Drawn tracks up to 5 km (rule drawn-lap-length-max); an imported track's is informational (its centreline's length), up to 7 km (Bedford Autodrome GT, 5.9 km).

gridSize.title: Grid size
gridSize.description: Number of grid slots (cars), laid out two abreast.

weathers.title: Weathers
weathers.description: Weathers offered for this track (at least one).

CrossingFacts.title: Crossing facts
CrossingFacts.description: Facts for an annotated crossing that matches a real crossing. Annotations listed in unmatchedCrossingAnnotations have no entry.

nearestJumpM.description: Distance along either branch from the crossing to the nearest jump or ramp. Absent when neither branch has a jump or ramp.

availableRampLengthM.description: For a bridge: the shortest run available on the over branch for a ramp up or down.

rampGradePct.description: For a bridge: peak grade (%) of its ramps, after climbing high enough to clear the under branch's local height.

heightStepM.description: For a flat crossing: difference between the two branches' marker-defined heights before they are levelled to meet.

MarkerFeature.title: Marker feature
MarkerFeature.description: A feature a height marker sits on: the start grid area or a bridge ramp.

sM.description: Distance along the marker's route (from the start/finish on the main loop, from the start join on an alternative route).

gradePct.description: Steepest sustained grade (%) the marker demands: the larger height change per distance to its neighbouring markers or anchors.

feature.description: Set when the marker sits on the grid area or a bridge ramp; absent otherwise.

startGapM.description: Distance from the route's start to the main loop, before snapping.

endGapM.description: Distance from the route's end to the main loop, before snapping.

UnannotatedCrossing.title: Unannotated crossing
UnannotatedCrossing.description: A place where the track crosses itself that no crossing annotation marks.

x.description: Canvas x of the crossing, so the UI can place a marker there.

GeometryFacts.title: Geometry facts
GeometryFacts.description: Measurements computed by the geometry service (trackgen_geom) from the scaled layout. The rules engine compares them against thresholds in track-rules.json; it never computes geometry itself.

firstSectorLengthM.description: Clear road ahead of the start/finish line available for the grid: up to the first tight corner, crossing, jump, ramp or alternative-route junction. The grid sits here, ahead of the line, and the first checkpoint follows the last grid row.

maxAbsCoordinateM.description: Largest |x| or |y| of any track geometry after centring and scaling.

minCornerRadiusM.description: Tightest centreline corner radius after smoothing.

crossings.description: Per-crossing facts, keyed by crossing id.

unannotatedCrossings.description: Places where the track crosses itself that no annotation marks. Always reported by the geometry core (possibly empty).

unmatchedCrossingAnnotations.description: Ids of crossing annotations that match no place where the track crosses itself. Always reported by the geometry core (possibly empty).

altRoutes.description: Per-alternative-route facts, keyed by route id.

elevationMarkers.description: Per-height-marker facts, keyed by marker id (markers on a route that was built).

gridWidthM.description: Narrowest road width along the main grid (imported tracks with per-point widths; otherwise not reported and options.widthM applies).

gridMaxGradePct.description: Steepest grade (%) of the marker-defined height profile within the grid area (custom: the whole profile; presets: the markers' bumps; imported: the road).

heightRangeM.description: Highest minus lowest road surface height over all routes.

maxGradePct.description: Steepest road grade (%) over 10 m of any route (jumps and bridge ramps included).

maxBankDeg.description: Largest road cross-slope (camber or banking), degrees.
